# Psalm 110 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Translator:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** A Psalm of David. The LORD says to my Lord: "Sit at my right hand, until I make your enemies your footstool."

**2** The LORD sends forth from Zion your mighty scepter. Rule in the midst of your enemies!

**3** Your people will offer themselves freely on the day of your power, in holy garments; from the womb of the morning, the dew of your youth will be yours.

**4** The LORD has sworn and will not change his mind, "You are a priest forever after the order of Melchizedek."

**5** The Lord is at your right hand; he will shatter kings on the day of his wrath.

**6** He will execute judgment among the nations, filling them with corpses; he will shatter chiefs over the wide earth.

**7** He will drink from the brook by the way; therefore he will lift up his head.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Psalm 110.

- **110:3** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **110:7** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **110:5** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **110:2** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **110:6** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

- **110:1** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS restructures for English clarity; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary application.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **110:1**: Ne'um YHWH la'adoni — 'Utterance-of YHWH to-my-lord' — the most-cited OT verse in the NT (Matt 22:44, Acts 2:34, Heb 1:13). David's lord is greater than David.
- **110:4**: Melchizedek — priest-king of Salem (Gen 14:18). The combining of priestly and royal roles in one figure is unique and foundational for Hebrews 5-7.

### LOGOS
- **110:1**: The most quoted and alluded-to OT verse in the New Testament. Jesus uses it to challenge the Pharisees' understanding of the Messiah (Matt 22:41-46). The 'lord' who sits at YHWH's right hand is both Davidic and more than Davidic.
- **110:4**: The 'order of Melchizedek' combines kingship and priesthood — roles kept strictly separate in Israel (Saul was punished for presuming priestly functions). This psalm envisions a figure who legitimately holds both offices.

### PNEUMA
- **110:1**: This is the single most important messianic psalm in the entire Bible. Jesus himself quoted it to prove that the Messiah is more than just a human descendant of David — he's David's Lord. The NT references it more than any other OT verse.
- **110:4**: A priest forever, in the order of Melchizedek — not Aaron. This mysterious figure from Genesis 14 had no recorded genealogy, which made him the perfect type for a priesthood that transcends Israel's Levitical system. The book of Hebrews builds its entire theology of Jesus' priesthood on this single verse.

— SOPHIA
